quickAnswer.question: Is there an API to get YouTube transcripts?
quickAnswer.answer: YouTube's official Data API can only download captions for videos you own, and it requires OAuth sign-in. To get the transcript of any public YouTube video, use a YouTube transcript API such as TranscriptX: send the video URL and receive the transcript with timestamps, in over 100 languages. If the video has no captions, TranscriptX transcribes the audio instead.

sections.h2: What Is a YouTube Transcript API?
content: A YouTube transcript API is a web service that returns the spoken text of a YouTube video to your code. You send a video URL or ID; you get back the transcript as text or structured data, usually split into timed segments.

Developers use it wherever video needs to become data: feeding lectures into a RAG pipeline, summarising videos with an LLM, generating subtitles, building search over a channel, or tracking what is said about a brand. Watching and copying by hand does not scale past a handful of videos — a YouTube video transcript API does.
TranscriptX gives you that in one call, and the same API also accepts TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and other links, plus audio and video files.

sections.h2: Why the Official YouTube API Can't Get Transcripts
content: Most developers start with the YouTube Data API, search for "youtube api get transcript", "youtube api get video transcript" or "youtube api get captions", and hit the same wall. The Data API does have a captions resource — you can list caption tracks and call captions.download — but downloading only works for videos you own or manage, and every request needs OAuth authorisation from that channel. For anyone else's video, the official YouTube API transcript route simply is not available.

There are other limits too. The Data API returns caption files, not transcripts: if a video has no captions, there is nothing to download. Auto-generated captions are often missing punctuation and speaker turns. And every call counts against a daily quota.

A YouTube transcript API like TranscriptX solves the problem from the other side. It works from the public video itself, needs no owner permission and no OAuth flow, and when captions are missing it transcribes the audio — so every public video returns text.

items.content: Caption tracks for your own videos only, OAuth required, no transcript when captions do not exist, daily quota.
Any public video, no OAuth, transcribes audio when captions are missing, timestamps and speaker labels, SRT/VTT output.

content: If what you need is subtitles rather than plain text, the same request covers it. As a YouTube captions API, TranscriptX returns timed segments you can render as captions in your own player; as a YouTube subtitles API, it exports ready-made SRT or VTT files you can load into an editor, a video platform or a translation workflow.

Because the subtitles are generated from the audio, you get them even for videos that have no caption track — the case where "youtube api get subtitles", "youtube api subtitles" and "youtube api captions download" return nothing.

Many YouTube transcript tools only read the caption track YouTube already has. That works until you hit a video with captions disabled, a fresh upload that has not been auto-captioned yet, or a language YouTube does not caption — and then you get an error instead of a transcript.

TranscriptX transcribes the audio itself, so caption availability stops being your problem. Background music and noise are separated from speech first, every speaker is labelled, and on clear audio our internal tests measure around 95% word accuracy.
Length is not a constraint either: an hour of audio takes about 1–2 minutes, and we have tested single 10-hour recordings, which matters for lectures, podcasts and livestream replays.

items.q: Does YouTube have an official transcript API?
items.a: Not for public videos. The YouTube Data API can download caption tracks only for videos you own or manage, with OAuth authorisation. To get transcripts of other public videos, you need a third-party YouTube transcript API.

items.q: How do I get YouTube transcript API access?
items.a: Create a TranscriptX account and generate an API key — the steps and code examples are at the top of this page. Then send any public YouTube URL to get its transcript.

items.q: What happens if a YouTube video has no captions?
items.a: TranscriptX transcribes the audio, so you still get a full transcript with timestamps and speaker labels.

items.q: Can I get YouTube captions and subtitles as SRT or VTT?
items.a: Yes. Transcripts can be exported as SRT or VTT subtitle files, as well as plain text.
Over 100 languages, detected automatically from the audio.

items.q: Does it work with YouTube Shorts and live replays?
items.a: Yes, as long as the video is public. A live stream can be transcribed once it has ended and the replay is available.

items.q: Can I transcribe private or unlisted videos?
items.a: No. Private, unlisted and sign-in-only videos are not supported.

items.q: How long does a long video take?
items.a: About 1–2 minutes per hour of audio. We have tested single recordings of 10 hours.
